title: A Detention for the Prom
premise: Jonah Sterling, the varsity team's statistician, has quietly discovered that the school board has been falsifying eligibility records to keep star players on the field — and that his own late father's name is buried in the cover-up. When his teacher pairs him with Priya Raman, the student journalist he's feuded with since freshman year, for a semester-long archival project, their research keeps colliding with the same sealed files. Forced into an uneasy alliance, they race to expose the truth before the championship game, when the board plans to destroy the remaining records. At the prom — held the night before the final game — they go public, and Jonah must choose between protecting his father's legacy and telling the whole truth.
about_author: Felix Sterling is a former high school math tutor who spent three seasons keeping stats for a small-town football team, where he learned that numbers never lie but people do. He writes stories about kids who are smarter than the adults in charge.

chapters.title: The Numbers Don't Cheer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Opening at a Friday night game, Jonah runs the stats and notices an impossible pattern: two ineligible players on the roster. He tells himself it's a clerical error. The emotional beat is denial — establishing his voice of anxious rationalization and his 'everything is fine' mantra as cracks begin to show.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In AP Research, Mr. Okafor pairs Jonah with Priya Raman, his nemesis since she published an unflattering article about the team in freshman year. Their first project meeting devolves into old grievances until Priya mentions she's been requesting board minutes that keep coming back redacted. Beat: reluctant curiosity replacing hostility.

chapters.title: Redacted
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Working in the school archive, they discover the redactions all cluster around one season — five years ago, the year Jonah's father coached. Priya treats it as a story; Jonah feels it as a threat. They agree to dig anyway, each hiding their real motive from the other. Beat: uneasy partnership forged in shared obsession.

chapters.title: What Dad Kept in the Garage
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Searching his father's boxes, Jonah finds a flash drive labeled only 'IF SOMETHING HAPPENS.' It contains eligibility forms with forged signatures — including his father's. Jonah pockets the drive without telling Priya. Beat: guilt and protectiveness; the first lie inside the alliance.

chapters.title: The Booster Club Smile
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya requests an interview with Superintendent Vance and gets charmed, deflected, and subtly threatened — her college recommendation letter suddenly depends on 'school spirit.' She realizes someone is watching their project. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance; she suspects Jonah is holding something back.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Someone ransacks Jonah's locker and takes his stat notebook. Coach Delgado warns him off 'digging up things that hurt people who loved your dad.' Jonah wavers — was his father complicit or a whistleblower? Beat: isolation; he pushes Priya away just as they need each other most.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Jonah about the drive; he finally confesses everything, including that his father may have signed the forgeries. Instead of anger, she shows him a scanned letter she found: his father anonymously tipped off the board whistleblower hotline the week he died. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve; real trust at last.

chapters.title: The Last Home Game Problem
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They map the full scheme: Vance and the boosters have been recycling ineligible players for years, and the records room is scheduled for 'renovation' the Monday after championships. With days left, they draft the exposé but can't verify the final document without breaking into the archive. Beat: ticking clock; dread and determination.

chapters.title: Prom Night
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At prom, while everyone dances, Jonah and Priya slip into the records wing using Priya's press pass. They photograph the master ledger — and are nearly caught by Vance himself, who offers Jonah a scholarship-shaped bribe. Jonah refuses on the record, phone recording in his pocket. Beat: climax; courage over fear, love confessed in a stairwell after.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine (Actually)
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The story breaks the morning of the championship; the game proceeds under protest, the season vacated, Vance resigning by June. Jonah testifies that his father tried to stop it, reclaiming his dad's memory honestly. At a rescheduled, unofficial dance in the gym, Jonah and Priya finally just get to be seventeen. Beat: resolution; truth as a form of love.
